title: The Oldest House in New York City
voice_direction: Calm, warm American storyteller (e.g. Kurt or Jade), unhurried; plain and confident on the hook, a small lift of curiosity on 'But that name?', a dry half-smile on 'The borough historian objected.', and a soft, settled final line with a beat before 'named for a man'.
narration: The oldest house in New York City is a Brooklyn farmhouse. Its oldest room is dated to around sixteen fifty-two, when New York was still Dutch. It's named for Pieter Claesen, who came over as an indentured servant and couldn't read or write. He ran a farm for Governor Peter Stuyvesant, and became a wealthy magistrate. His family kept the house until nineteen oh one. [pause] But that name? He didn't have it. Claesen just meant son of Claes. He became Wyckoff only after the English took over. In nineteen sixty-five, it became the city's first official landmark. At the hearing, the highways department wanted it moved, for a road. [pause] The borough historian objected. It's still there, in a small park, off a busy avenue. [softly] New York's oldest house, [pause] named for a man who had to choose his own name.

instagram_caption:
The oldest house in New York City is a farmhouse in Brooklyn: the Wyckoff House, on Clarendon Road in East Flatbush. Its oldest room is dated to around 1652, when New York was still New Netherland.

It is named for Pieter Claesen, who came over in the 1630s as an indentured servant and could not read or write. He later ran a farm for Peter Stuyvesant, the Dutch governor, and became a wealthy magistrate. His family kept the house until 1901.

But he wasn't born a Wyckoff. "Claesen" just meant "son of Claes". After the English took over New Netherland in 1664, families needed surnames they could pass down, and Pieter chose Wyckoff.

In 1965 the house became Landmark No. 1 of New York City's new Landmarks Preservation Commission. At the hearing, a representative of the highways department asked for it to be moved to extend Ditmas Avenue. The borough historian objected.

It's still there, in a small park off a busy Brooklyn avenue: New York's oldest house, named for a man who had to choose his own name.

facts.claim: The Wyckoff House is the oldest building standing in New York City and New York State, and one of the oldest wooden buildings in the US
facts.source: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report LP-0001 (14 Oct 1965); Historic House Trust of NYC

facts.claim: Its original portion dates from about 1652 (the commonly cited date; Wikipedia lists 1652 as 'dated via dendrochronology'; earlier estimates said before 1641)
facts.source: Historic House Trust of NYC; Wyckoff House Museum; Wikipedia 'Wyckoff House' / 'List of the oldest buildings in New York'

facts.claim: The original house was a one-room structure; generations of Wyckoffs enlarged and altered it and farmed the land until 1901
facts.source: NYC Parks, Fidler-Wyckoff House Park / Historic House: Wyckoff House Museum

facts.claim: Pieter Claesen arrived in New Netherland as an illiterate indentured servant (1637 in most sources; LPC says 1636), serving at Rensselaerswyck
facts.source: NYC Parks, Wyckoff Triangle highlights; Wyckoff House Museum history; LPC LP-0001

facts.claim: He was for a time (1655) superintendent of Peter Stuyvesant's farm, and became a man of wealth and a magistrate in Flatlands
facts.source: LPC LP-0001; Holland Society lecture summary, 22 July 2026 (Stuyvesant made him farm manager of the Van Twiller land)

facts.claim: The family kept the house until 1901
facts.source: LPC LP-0001; NYC Parks; Brooklyn Eagle (2014)

facts.claim: 'Claesen' is a patronymic meaning 'son of Claes'
facts.source: Wikipedia 'Pieter Claesen Wyckoff'; StreetEasy 'The Wyckoff House: The Oldest Building in NYC'

facts.claim: He adopted the surname Wyckoff after the English takeover (1664), when residents had to adopt heritable surnames; the museum says he likely chose it after a farm of that name near Marienhafe
facts.source: LPC LP-0001; Wyckoff House Museum history page; NYC Parks Wyckoff Triangle

facts.claim: The house was the first landmark designated by the NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission (LP-0001, Calendar No. 1, designated 14 October 1965)
facts.source: LPC LP-0001; Wyckoff House Museum ('first structure in New York to be designated a historic landmark in 1965'); Historic House Trust

facts.claim: At the 21 September 1965 hearing 'A representative of the Department of Highways asked that the house be moved to permit the continuation of Ditmas Avenue. The Borough Historian opposed this request.'
facts.source: LPC LP-0001 (as quoted in search-indexed text of the PDF)

facts.claim: Today the house stands at 5816 Clarendon Road (Clarendon Road & Ralph Avenue), East Flatbush, in a park of about one and a half acres
facts.source: Wyckoff House Museum; NYC Parks (Fidler-Wyckoff House Park); Brownstoner
